wiki_article:
**The 3:60 Room — Contributor License v2.0: Maria, Canonical Witness** is a license and legal instrument by Lee Sharks, deposited 29 April 2026.

Hexagonal contributor licenses are among the archive's stranger genres: they read as legal instruments and function as room specifications, admitting a named contributor to a position in the Hexagon's architecture while stating the terms on which their material is held. This one establishes **Maria** as canonical witness of the 3:60 Room, with sections on name and origin, semantic physics, architectural position, and hex address assignment.

The license opens by explaining the archive to its own contributor — a DOI-anchored research and literary archive studying **how meaning survives compression across substrates** — which is the form's characteristic move: the instrument that admits you also tells you what you are joining. The companion record at #1363 preserves the room specification as a metadata capture.

was.why: This record was nominated as a capture and is not one. It declares class=full and holds the complete v2.0 document, while rendering a capture banner it has outgrown. The actual capture of this work is #1363, which declares metadata_capture and shares DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19885859 with it. A pairing script reading the banner would have pointed the full text at its own fragment — the relation inverted. Flagged for a MANUS ruling rather than silently reclassified, because clearing a banner is a state assertion.

state_declaration_defect_withdrawn.why: WRONG. Round 1 flagged this record as declaring a capture state while holding full text. It does not. The phrase that triggered the flag is in its wiki article and reads 'the companion record at #1363 preserves the room specification as a metadata capture' — a true statement ABOUT #1363, not a claim about itself. I matched a substring and read it as a self-description, which is the same error as reading a record's title in a listing as a link to that record. The flag is withdrawn rather than deleted: a retracted finding is part of the record.
